text:
maya: Heads-up — SRE + Product sync: need to settle prioritization for next sprint. Main tradeoff: protect SLOs vs shipping high-impact features (customer-driven). Proposing we use a RICE-ish cutoff + explicit toil burn-down weight. Thoughts?

jon: +1. Can we see concrete examples? RICE helps but we should anchor Reach in queries/day or affected customers not just %s.

sam: customer asks: dedicated capacity for AcmeCorp (they're hitting tail latency). Big $ and retention impact if we don't. Impact high, effort is non-trivial (infra + billing changes).

li: From oncall: ~45% of P1s last quarter were KV cache misses and autoscaler flaps. If we invest in durability and autoscaler fixes, that reduces toil and incident MTTR. Toil reduction is real long-term velocity gain.

alex: Launch criteria note: if we delay dedicated capacity, can we temporarily relax SLO from 99.95 -> 99.9 for that customer region while we ship? needs legal + sales OK.

jon: If useful, quick RICE math for two candidates:
- Initiative A (SLO hardening autoscale): Reach=30k user req/day, Impact=7, Confidence=0.7, Effort=25 engineer-weeks -> RICE ~ (30*7*0.7)/25 = 5.88
- Initiative B (Dedicated capacity offering): Reach=5k requests (paying), Impact=9, Confidence=0.6, Effort=40 -> RICE ~ (5*9*0.6)/40 = 0.675
This shows raw RICE favors SLO work unless we weight paying customers higher.

maya: Exactly — raw RICE misses strategic customer value and toil amortization. Proposal: compute two scores: 1) RICE_raw, 2) RICE_biz where Reach for paying customers is multiplied by 5 and add toil-savings as an "effort discount" (reduce Effort by % equal to expected toil reduction over 6 months).

li: Practical example: autoscale fix reduces weekly pager pages by ~30% => estimate saving ~6 engineer-weeks over 6 months. If effort for that initiative is 25, effective effort becomes 19 (25-6). That bumps RICE to ~7.7 in jon's calc.

sam: For sales-led deals we should also add a Qualifier: contract value > $100k/year -> auto-priority. Otherwise use RICE_biz threshold 10 to queue for next sprint.

alex: On SLO relaxation: ops + legal + sales alignment needed. I can take sales loop. We shouldn't relax cluster-wide SLOs, only customer-specific routing with clear TTL and rollback.

jon: Also recommend we enforce a "toil tax" in planning: reserve 10% sprint capacity for toil elimination/infra projects until we hit target MTTR/alert counts. Helps stop feature-only hacks.

ops-bot: deploy: canary of autoscaler-fix v2 started on staging at 2025-11-09T14:12:18Z :rocket:

maya: Next steps: 1) jon to draft RICE_biz spreadsheet and example calculations by EOD tomorrow. 2) alex to confirm legal constraints for per-customer SLO relax. 3) li to quantify toil savings from autoscale + cache improvements (est engineer-weeks). 4) sam to list top 3 commercial deals impacted. We'll reconvene Thurs 10am. If anyone objects to the scoring adjustments speak now.

li: noted, I'll attach incident counts and pager-duty exports to the doc.

sam: listing deals now and pinging sales for ARR numbers.

jon: will mock-up spreadsheet and include quick calc for RICE_biz and toil discount.

maya: thanks. aim is to get alignment so PMs can negotiate scope (can defer non-critical UX, etc.) while protecting platform SLOs. :thumbsup:

alex: +1. if we need to sequence, prefer SLO-first for core infra then customer-specific features behind feature flags.

maya: perfect — see you Thu 10. I'll post agenda.
